two_sheet_coordinates.endpoint_line: L_end=span(1,1), the +1 parity line of R_0

green_geometry.maximality: each is a one-dimensional maximal isotropic line in C^2

pauli_sewing.meaning: the sewing changes reciprocal parity exactly once, converting the odd forcing amplitude into the even matched endpoint channel

full_forcing_ports.norms: reflection with the minus phase is unitary on the full L2 forcing-port carrier

compatibility.unitary_intertwiner: Pauli Z supplies the finite parity-changing seam map
compatibility.relation_to_prior_pauli_module: this is the same algebraic role as the response quarter-turn/Pauli covariance, now applied to source-versus-endpoint parity lines

remaining_gate.not_yet: a single unitary feedback operator on the complete doubled colligation ports whose restriction is Z on amplitude/endpoint lines and -R on forcing-history features
remaining_gate.test: assemble its block matrix and verify the polarized Gram identity on arbitrary pairs of source-generated states, not only on the Xi kernel line
remaining_gate.danger: linewise isometry does not guarantee compatibility of mixed endpoint-forcing pairings

conclusion: The reflected source-sign obstruction is not fatal: the odd source line and even Xi endpoint line are both maximal isotropic and are canonically related by Pauli Z. This provides the finite parity-changing component required of reciprocal feedback. The unresolved part is its extension over the mixed full-tail ports.
